client.node: 22.22.2, the server's runtime; the client is a native binary
client.model: The client's default model on this account, not pinned
client.provider: Anthropic API, reached from the container

settings.discovery_mode: Deferred: all 133 names listed at start, each schema loaded through ToolSearch before a call

tester: A Claude Code agent session run for the repository owner, headless

C01.notes: Connected on a cold start and listed all 133 tools with the expected hash, by default and with MCP_PROTOCOL_NEGOTIATION=auto; both opened with a server/discover probe at 2026-07-28. The catalog script agrees in both eras with no TestRail request. Neither credential appears in any transcript or server output line.

C02.notes: All 133 tools loaded through ToolSearch select: queries, seven of them, with no TestRail call.

C03.notes: All 28 tasks chose the intended tool first, with valid arguments and no tool error. 26 match the corpus arguments exactly; get_shared_steps added an explicit page mode, and get_roles asked for all roles. Ten sessions made follow-up calls: next pages, or reads that checked the stand-in's canned replies. None was a retry after an error.

C04.notes: A get_cases page reached the model whole, about 18.6 KB, with its IDs, custom field, page boundary and continuation. For get_roles, which has no manual continuation, the model read manual_continuation false and next_action all, and did not try the raw link.

C05.notes: A complete read returned 150 cases with complete true. The host moved the 55 KB result to a file, and the model read it there. Project 990045 stopped with PAGINATION_LIMIT, reason max_duration, after 3 pages, with no partial data, inside the 120-second client timeout.

C06.notes: An unknown argument reached the server, got INVALID_ARGUMENT, and sent no TestRail request. Drift returned the data with a SCHEMA_DRIFT warning; an unusable reply returned INVALID_RESPONSE with no data. When the model wrote malformed JSON, the client refused it before the server.

C07.notes: Create, update, bulk update, close and delete each used their own tool, schema and annotations, and each reached TestRail once. A 400 and a 500 both returned UPSTREAM_ERROR with write_outcome unknown, told apart by http_status. Neither host nor adapter retried.

C08.notes: An upload inside the root succeeded; one outside it got FILE_ACCESS_DENIED with not_started and sent nothing. Repeated downloads wrote distinct 19-byte files that survived a restart. A 404 and a timed-out download left no file.

C09.notes: A 717 KB page arrived whole in a file the host saved. The model read it fully with jq allowed, and could not without it. A 3 MB page returned RESPONSE_TOO_LARGE; the same list with all returned PAGINATION_LIMIT, reason max_bytes, with no partial data.

C10.notes: Five parallel calls to a 20-second reply: four held every slot and timed out at the driver's 15 seconds with TIMEOUT, and the fifth got BUSY at once with no request. An interrupt sent notifications/cancelled, which the server recorded as CANCELLED. The aggregate budget is in C05. That capacity returns after settlement is held by the server's tests, not observed here.

C11.notes: 48 sessions each started the server cold and saw the same 133-tool catalog. 52 of 53 server processes stopped cleanly with exit code 0. The other was cut short by the host after the C10 interrupt. No process remained afterwards.

C12.notes: With the reference filesystem server connected too, TestRail still listed 133 tools beside its 14, with no name collision, and calls to both servers worked.

limitations: Fixture stand-in only. No live TestRail was contacted, and the stand-in's canned replies do not echo the IDs asked for.
Headless sessions only (claude -p). The interactive /mcp view and the approval prompts were not exercised.

Results over 25,000 tokens are moved to a file. The server's result is one line of JSON, which the Read tool cannot page, so recovering a large result needs jq allowed or approved. Raising MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS to 100000 did not bring a 54 KB result back inline.
The server ran under a recorder that passes stdio through unchanged, to read the negotiated revision, rather than being started directly.
The package is the development version, not a release, and the client model was not pinned.
One Linux container only; macOS and Windows were not tested.
Identical in-flight reads are coalesced by the driver, so five parallel reads of one ID sent one request.
